extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's 'The Rising Sea')
extracted.subtask_description: Develop and prove versions of Serre duality (vector-bundle, Hom, and Ext versions), define and recognize dualizing sheaves/trace maps, and check these statements in key examples such as projective space; understand the role of Cohen–Macaulay hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinant of the cotangent bundle is dualizing for smooth varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: Desideratum: the determinant of the cotangent bundle is dualizing for smooth varieties. If X is smooth, we want ωX = KX (recall KX = det ΩX) — i.e., the canonical bundle should be Serre-dualizing (and in particular ωX is invertible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is identified as a key desideratum but is noted to be harder to prove than the basic duality statements; later exercises (e.g. 30.4.I, 30.4.H) address when ωX is invertible (e.g., regular embeddings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial Serre duality for vector bundles
rubrics_metrics.description: Desideratum: If F is locally free of finite rank on an n-dimensional projective k-scheme X, then there should be a functorial isomorphism Hi(X, F) ≅ H^{n−i}(X, F^∨ ⊗ ωX)^∨, functorial in F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently a natural isomorphism of covariant functors H^{n−i}(X, (·)^∨ ⊗ ωX) → Hi(X, ·)^∨. The text aims to construct a particular isomorphism and notes that this functorial version will follow from the trace/cup-product construction when X is Cohen–Macaulay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace version of Serre duality for vector bundles
rubrics_metrics.description: Desideratum (trace version): There should be a cup product Hi(X, F) × H^{n−i}(X, F^∨ ⊗ ωX) → H^n(X, ωX) together with a trace map t : H^n(X, ωX) → k, such that the resulting pairing Hi(X, F) × H^{n−i}(X, F^∨ ⊗ ωX) → k is perfect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The trace/cup-product construction is the expected origin of the functorial isomorphism; the text notes the trace version (and hence functorial version) holds when X is Cohen–Macaulay (in particular smooth). An indication of proving the trace version is given later (Remark 30.3.15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial Serre duality for Hom
rubrics_metrics.description: Desideratum: For any coherent sheaf F on a pure n-dimensional projective k-scheme X there should be a functorial isomorphism Hom(F, ωX) ≅ H^n(X, F)^∨ (functorial in F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a weaker duality than the vector-bundle version but applies without Cohen–Macaulay hypotheses. The text introduces this as 'Serre duality for Hom' and explains how it relates to the trace version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace version of Serre duality for Hom (perfect pairing requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition/Desideratum: A coherent sheaf ωX with a map t : H^n(X, ωX) → k is dualizing (for Hom) if for every coherent F the natural map Hom(F, ωX) × H^n(X, F) → H^n(X, ωX) →^t k is a perfect pairing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition (30.1.4) explicitly packages the data (ωX, t); if such data exist they define Serre duality for Hom. The text also states that the functorial version implies the trace version (Exercise 30.1.A), and vice versa in this Hom context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of the dualizing sheaf and trace
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition: If a dualizing sheaf and trace (ωX, t) exists for X, this data is unique up to unique isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof sketched: two dualizing pairs induce natural bijections Hom(F, ωX) ≅ Hom(F, ωX') functorially in F, hence by a universal property there is a unique isomorphism ωX ≅ ωX' carrying t to t'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre duality holds for projective space (Pn)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete case: For P^n_k with ω_{P^n} ≅ O_{P^n}(-n-1) and a chosen isomorphism t : H^n(P^n, ω) ≅ k, the natural map Hom(F, ω) → H^n(P^n, F)^∨ is a perfect pairing (i.e., Serre duality for Hom holds for P^n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives exercises and a proposition (30.1.7) proving the functorial version for P^n: reduce to sums of line bundles using a resolution F: 0→G→E→F→0 with E a sum of O(m)'s, compare exact sequences and use Five Lemma variants. Exercise 30.1.B checks the line-bundle cases by hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial Serre duality for Ext (stronger Ext-version)
rubrics_metrics.description: Desideratum/definition: There should be isomorphisms Ext^i(·, ωX) ≅ H^{n−i}(X, ·)^∨ (functorial in the coherent sheaf argument). If such isomorphisms hold for all i, X satisfies functorial Serre duality for Ext.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Ext-version generalizes both the vector-bundle and Hom versions. The text explains that proving the functorial Ext-version (plus Desideratum 30.1.1 about ωX when X is smooth) suffices to derive the vector-bundle Serre duality results. It also states functorial Serre duality for Ext holds for projective space (30.1.10), using universal δ-functor arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace version of Serre duality for Ext (cup product expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Desideratum: There should be a natural cup product Ext^i(F, ωX) × H^{n−i}(X, F) → H^n(X, ωX) which composed with the trace t : H^n(X, ωX) → k gives a perfect pairing realizing the Ext-version of duality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text notes it will not construct this cup product in full generality here, but indicates how one should expect the trace version to arise and that the functorial Ext-version should follow from the trace/cup-product picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohen–Macaulay hypotheses are often necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Warning/necessity statement: Cohen–Macaulay hypotheses are necessary where stated. Example: the union of two 2-planes in P^4_k meeting at a point does not admit a coherent dualizing sheaf with the expected Serre duality consequences (cohomology contradictions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The example (30.1.12 and exercise 30.1.E) shows failure of Serre duality without Cohen–Macaulay: Serre vanishing would force certain H^i to vanish if a dualizing sheaf existed, but explicit computation shows they do not; hence CM hypotheses cannot be dropped in general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial/trace implication relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Logical relations among variants: (a) For Hom: the functorial version implies the trace version (Exercise 30.1.A). (b) For vector bundles: the trace version (cup product + trace) implies the functorial version, and both hold when X is Cohen–Macaulay (hence smooth). (c) For Ext: the functorial Ext-version implies the vector-bundle functorial version (Exercise 30.2.I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These implication notes guide which statements need proving to obtain others: e.g., proving functorial Serre duality for Ext (and Det(Ω) = ωX for smooth X) yields classical vector-bundle Serre duality. The text points to exercises demonstrating these formal implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective-space proof strategy via resolutions and δ-functors
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof recipe for P^n: present any coherent F by 0→G→E→F→0 with E a finite sum of line bundles; use Hom(·, ω) applied to the sequence and the long exact cohomology sequence dualized to compare and deduce the isomorphism Hom(F, ω) ≅ H^n(F)^∨ by Five Lemma arguments and checking line-bundle base cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the concrete method used to establish Serre duality for Hom and Ext on P^n: check base cases (line bundles) by hand (Exercise 30.1.B), then bootstrap via resolutions and universal δ-functor arguments (Exercises 30.1.C/D).
